claims.text: As-deposited AlCrTiZrMo films have a less-developed oxide layer than the proposed annealed films.
Annealing AlCrTiZrMo at 800 °C for 1 hour in air induces formation of ZrTiO4.
The annealing-induced ZrTiO4 forms a dense oxide layer.
The ZrTiO4-containing oxide layer is robust and adherent under sliding.
The ZrTiO4-containing oxide layer minimizes mechanical spallation.
The ZrTiO4-containing oxide layer acts as a barrier against corrosive ingress.
The annealed oxide layer reduces friction by lowering local deformation.
The oxide layer limits exposure of fresh alloy material to the corrosive environment during sliding.
Maintaining oxide-layer integrity decouples mechanical wear from corrosive degradation.
Annealed films with an intact oxide layer will show smaller OCP variations than as-deposited films.
Annealed films with an intact oxide layer will have lower friction coefficients than as-deposited films.
Annealed films with an intact oxide layer will have lower wear rates than as-deposited films.
Annealing will reduce total degradation under combined wear and corrosion relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The protective effect will persist only while sliding stresses remain below the oxide layer's adhesion or failure strength.
Very high mechanical stresses can cause oxide-layer spallation and nullify its protective effect.
Extremely aggressive corrosive environments can degrade the oxide layer and nullify its protective effect.
Prior evidence indicates that dense oxide layers can improve both corrosion resistance and wear resistance.
